title: The Character I Almost Overlooked: Shebna
paragraphs: The Character I Almost Overlooked: Shebna

He had the office.
The title.
The access.
And still, God called him out by name.
A palace official. A manager in the king’s house. Not a giant. Not a prophet. Not a king. Just a man close to power.
But that was the danger.

In Isaiah 22:15–19, the Lord confronts Shebna because he turned stewardship into self-exaltation. He carved out a grand tomb for himself. He lived like his name deserved to outlast his obedience. He held a sacred responsibility, but somewhere along the way, platform became his idol.
That hits hard.

Because not everyone falls through open rebellion.
Some fall through polished ambition.
Through spiritual image management.
Through wanting to be seen more than wanting to be faithful.

Shebna’s sin was deeper than pride.
It was misusing what belonged to God to build himself.
And that still happens now.

A ministry can become a monument.
A gift can become a throne.
A calling can become a brand.
And a servant of God can slowly start acting like the house is his.
But here’s what we miss:

The story of Shebna is not just about judgment.
It is about ownership.

The position was never his.
The authority was never his.
The glory was never his.

God removed Shebna and raised up Eliakim, showing that He alone appoints and He alone uproots. The Lord is not impressed by titles worn without trembling. Heaven does not bow to our résumé. God looks for faithful hands, not inflated names.
And that’s where grace walks in.
Because if Shebna exposes the disease, Jesus reveals the cure.

We have all, in some way, tried to build ourselves with what God gave us.
We have all wanted control, applause, permanence.
But Christ did the opposite. He had all authority, yet He humbled Himself. He did not grasp for glory. He poured Himself out, went to the cross, and rose again to save proud people like us.
That means even the Shebna-hearted can repent.

You do not have to keep performing.
You do not have to keep protecting your image.
You do not have to build a monument out of your own name.
Lay it down.

Jesus is still rescuing people who made themselves too big and God too small.
Jesus is still cleansing ambition.
Jesus is still teaching servants how to kneel again.

So before you ask, “What position do I hold?”
Ask, “Am I still faithful in the house?”
Because the most dangerous thing is not obscurity.
It is influence without surrender.

Read Isaiah 22:15–25 again.
Let it search you.
Then run to Christ.
